items.name: Honey bee
items.blurb: The bee that makes the honey we eat. A hive can hold tens of thousands of bees with one queen.

differences.common-wasp: The honey bee is furry and golden-brown with a rounded body; the common wasp is shiny, bright yellow and black, with a narrow waist.
differences.marmalade-hoverfly: The hoverfly has one pair of wings, big eyes, short stubby antennae and hovers still; the honey bee has two pairs of wings and longer antennae.

clues: Workers do a "waggle dance" to show others where flowers are.
A worker dies after stinging a person because its sting is barbed.
Its wax is used for candles and polish.
It lives in a colony with a queen.
It lives in hives looked after by beekeepers.
It makes a sweet golden food spread on toast.

differences.dark-edged-bee-fly: The bee-fly has a long straight beak, one pair of dark-edged wings and hovers to feed; the bumblebee has two pairs of wings and lands on flowers.

clues: It is used in greenhouses to pollinate tomatoes.
It shivers its flight muscles to warm up.

It lives in a colony with a queen.

questions.prompt: How many legs does a bee have?
questions.explain: Bees are insects, and all insects have six legs.

questions.prompt: What do honey bees make that people eat?
questions.explain: They turn flower nectar into honey to feed the hive.

questions.prompt: A honey bee worker usually dies after stinging a person.
questions.explain: Its barbed sting stays in our skin and tears away from the bee.
Hoverflies are harmless flies that copy wasp colours.

questions.prompt: What does a honey bee's "waggle dance" tell the other bees?
wrong: That it is time to sleep
questions.explain: The angle and length of the dance show direction and distance.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest wasp in the world?
questions.explain: Queens can be about 5 cm long.

questions.prompt: How can you tell a hoverfly from a wasp?
questions.answer: It has one pair of wings
questions.explain: Flies have one pair of wings; wasps and bees have two.

questions.prompt: What do common wasps build their nests from?
questions.explain: They mix wood fibres with saliva to make paper.

questions.prompt: Only female bees and wasps can sting.
questions.explain: The sting is a modified egg-laying tube, so males have none.

questions.prompt: In a honey bee hive, which bee lays the eggs?
questions.explain: One queen can lay over a thousand eggs a day.

questions.prompt: What do bees collect from flowers?
questions.explain: Nectar becomes honey; pollen feeds the young.
A hive can hold tens of thousands of bees.

questions.prompt: Bees help plants make seeds by carrying pollen from flower to flower.

questions.explain: The bright colours warn that they can sting.
